reference_authors: H W Nijman; J G Houbiers; M P Vierboom; S H van der Burg; J W Drijfhout; J D'Amaro; P Kenemans; C J Melief; W M Kast
reference_titles: Identification of peptide sequences that potentially trigger HLA-A2.1-restricted cytotoxic T lymphocytes.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The IIPSGPLKA peptide was incubated overnight with T2 cells. T2 cells were washed once and then stained by indirect immunofluorescence to determine upregulation of HLA-A2.1 expression on the cell surface. The fluoresence ratio (FR) was calculated with the formula: mean fluorescence experimental sample/mean fluorescence background. Data shown in quantitative field represents the FR for the peptide. Peptides with an FR > 1.5 were considered positive for binding to HLA-A2.1. The lack of HLA-A2.1 binding by the IIPSGPLKA peptide was consistent with its inability to block HLA-A2.1-restricted killing by a CTL clone in a competition cytotoxicity assay.
mhc_export.reference__title: Identification of peptide sequences that potentially trigger HLA-A2.1-restricted cytotoxic T lymphocytes.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: A computer scoring program based on the HLA-A2.1 peptide binding motif was used to score peptides within the influenza matrix protein for likelihood of binding to HLA-A2.1.
mhc_export.reference__authors: H W Nijman; J G Houbiers; M P Vierboom; S H van der Burg; J W Drijfhout; J D'Amaro; P Kenemans; C J Melief; W M Kast

mhc_export.assay__comments: The KLYRKLKREI peptide was incubated overnight with T2 cells. T2 cells were washed once and then stained by indirect immunofluorescence to determine upregulation of HLA-A2.1 expression on the cell surface. The fluoresence ratio (FR) was calculated with the formula: mean fluorescence experimental sample/mean fluorescence background. Data shown in quantitative field represents the FR for the peptide. Peptides with an FR > 1.5 were considered positive for binding to HLA-A2.1. The lack of HLA-A2.1 binding by the KLYRKLKREI peptide was consistent with its inability to block HLA-A2.1-restricted killing by a CTL clone in a competition cytotoxicity assay.

mhc_export.epitope__comments: A computer scoring program based on the HLA-A2.1 peptide binding motif was used to score peptides within the influenza matrix protein for likelihood of binding to HLA-A2.1. The sequence corresponds to residues 217-227 of  matrix protein 1 of some influenza strains, but is missing the T218 residue. An internal database source is provided here to account for the discrepancy between the published epitope sequence and the Matrix protein sequence currently available at public databases.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The EAMEVASQA peptide was incubated overnight with T2 cells. T2 cells were washed once and then stained by indirect immunofluorescence to determine upregulation of HLA-A2.1 expression on the cell surface. The fluoresence ratio (FR) was calculated with the formula: mean fluorescence experimental sample/mean fluorescence background. Data shown in quantitative field represents the FR for the peptide. Peptides with an FR > 1.5 were considered positive for binding to HLA-A2.1. The lack of HLA-A2.1 binding by the EAMEVASQA peptide was consistent with its inability to block HLA-A2.1-restricted killing by a CTL clone in a competition cytotoxicity assay.

mhc_export.assay__comments: Arbitrary units. The capacity of peptide M58 to promote HLA-A2 assembly, and the subsequent stability of peptide-MHC complexes was measured using an antibody specific for HLA-A2.  Peptide M58-66 promoted HLA-peptide complex formation to a degree similar to that seen with two variant peptides, including a retro-mouse pseudopeptide.  However, this peptide was less capable of conferring HLA-peptide stabilization than either variant (Leu59 or PMRI).
mhc_export.reference__title: A partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptide modulates the cytokine profile of CTL specific for an influenza virus epitope.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: Epitope M58-66 was previously defined and described.

mhc_export.assay__comments: Arbitrary units. HLA-A2 assembly and stabilization was measured using antibody specific for HLA-A2.  The capacity of peptide PRMI 58-59 to promote HLA-peptide complex  formation was similar to the wild-type peptide.  This peptide was also capable of conferring HLA-peptide stability (MFI = 200), which was 3-fold greater than the wild-type peptide.
mhc_export.reference__title: A partially modified retro-inverso pseudopeptide modulates the cytokine profile of CTL specific for an influenza virus epitope.
mhc_export.epitope__comments: The PRMI analog was derived from the wild-type M58-66 peptide of the influenza A virus matrix protein.  This analog peptide contained a leucine at position 59 (I to L) and the bond between residues 58 and 59 was modified to NH-CO instead of CO-NH.  This retro-inverso modification represents an isosteric replacement of the amide bonds which confers greater biological stability.
